name: Hassan Tower
hero_subtitle: Almohad minaret and vast esplanade of the unfinished 12th-century mosque.

overview.title: The unfinished masterpiece of the capital
overview.p1: Hassan Tower was meant to be the minaret of a vast Almohad mosque. Work stopped in the 12th century, leaving the red sandstone tower and a forest of incomplete columns on a wide esplanade. It remains one of Rabat’s defining silhouettes — especially paired with the modern Mohammed V Mausoleum beside it.
overview.p2: Allow time for security if you also visit the mausoleum. The site is open-air; bring sun protection at midday.

food.title: Eating near Hassan Tower
food.p1: Hotel and centre restaurants sit around the Hassan district. The site itself has limited food.
food.p2: Plan a meal before or after in Hassan or toward the medina.
food.li3: Medina tables a short taxi away.
food.li4: Water and hat essential at midday.
food.li5: L'Imprévu for a modern lunch in the centre.

q1.question: Can I climb the tower?
q1.answer: No — the interior is closed; enjoy it from the esplanade.

q2.question: How long?
q2.answer: Forty-five to ninety minutes with the mausoleum.

q3.question: Ticket needed?
q3.answer: Esplanade is free; follow signs for mausoleum access rules.

q4.question: Parking?
q4.answer: Limited — taxi or tram to the area is easier.

q5.question: Good for children?
q5.answer: Yes on the open square; watch sun exposure.
